repository.description: Java wrapper for native C++ UDT protocol.

issue.body:
Hi man,thanks for your great effort ,and when I was trying to check your code,and find out how to work with netty,the Echo Msg example always raise the exception,so does the netty 4 beta3.you may take a look at this .

Please take a look at it.
https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/1104

body: Thanks for your patience.  I've just pushed a fix.

@trustin Thanks very much,cause I am still learning the netty 4,so I don't know how to fix this issue ,sorry for the bother ,report this issue ,somehow make me as an idiot.
I just send an pull request to [webcam capture](https://github.com/sarxos/webcam-capture/tree/master/webcam-capture-examples/webcam-capture-live-streaming),which in the live stream example I am using netty3 to transport the stream package .Thanks for your great work.
and i detect an bug there.[need reorder the bytebuffer](https://github.com/sarxos/webcam-capture/blob/master/webcam-capture-examples/webcam-capture-live-streaming/src/main/java/us/sosia/video/stream/handler/H264StreamEncoder.java#L117)
When i transport this bytebuffer which default endian is little-endian,and then with the default implement of LengthFieldPrepender,will make the whole frame encoded channel buffer with the order same as the body.and then If i just transport this bytes to the remote peer.The remote's LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder will not work.
So i think how about add an bool flag to config the ByteOrder of the framecodec to use ,and do some reorder if it's necessary,and one more thing is could you please port the Bytebuf's order in netty4 to netty3 ,then make the channelbuffer could reorder too.
This issue is reported at:
I just think the netty framework should give out some information about this just like the channelbufferS.warp() did.
https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/1164
